pages.lesson:
LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 14.3.1 SENTENCES: DIRECT AND INDIRECT SPEECH

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.3: Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we report what others have said?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use the correct punctuation marks in direct speech

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. use the correct punctuation marks in direct speech
   In simple words: practise until you can use the correct punctuation marks in direct speech. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech in the examples.
2. Explain Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech.
4. Show that you can: use the correct punctuation marks in direct speech

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences: Direct and Indirect Speech important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read provided sentences or paragraphs to learn how direct and indirect speech appear in writing,
2. Communication and collaboration: It is enhanced as the learner works with others to complete exercises.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. use the correct punctuation marks in direct speech

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
